description: The list mid-edit: the bottom section has been moved up one place with the arrow, and the move is STAGED rather than saved. This scenario is DRIVEN — the capture clicks the row's Move up control rather than seeding a pre-moved order — because a staged change lives in the browser's pending-changes store, not in the markdown, and a scenario that only seeded a different order would prove nothing about staging. Its previous form seeded the same content as the plain in-order list and declared no interaction at all, so it was a byte-for-byte duplicate of that scenario whose description claimed a staged state its frame never actually showed; driving the click is what makes the two genuinely different. It is also the state that reveals the publish path: the markdown still holds the old numbers until Publish, so what changed here is the page's own state, and navigating away loses the arrangement while the pending change survives.
